We're currently speccing out first-class i18n behavior for Next.js, so this PR will probably be delayed until after that RFC is implemented since these two PRs overlap in scope:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/17078

Please add any feedback you may have on that RFC!

body: Amazing Work! but how do we generate static pages using getStaticProps?? Since JAMStack is biggest advantage of NEXT.js!
author: raghav0622

body: @raghav0622 In this example the data is behind user authentication, you can't pregenerate the content in that case, so it uses client side rendering instead, all the content is still static but the data is fetched in the client. If the data didn't depend on the user then you can go for `getStaticProps` 👍
author: lfades

body:
> @raghav0622 In this example the data is behind user authentication, you can't pregenerate the content in that case, so it uses client side rendering instead, all the content is still static but the data is fetched in the client. If the data didn't depend on the user then you can go for `getStaticProps` 👍

just a scenario where on build time all public data like blog posts or in this case movie titles can be fetched on build time in getStaticProps with anonymous authentication provided by realm-web (there is nodejs sdk just like firebase-admin), editing/upading relvanat data / blog posts is user-auth dependent

body:
> The common way of redirecting is fine, we don't have to match Express helpers. If redirecting is complicated then maybe we can mention it on docs instead and/or create an example for it.

Because so many people use Express and expect this helper (I myself was confused why it didn't exist) it would be wise to add it. It also solves a lot of problems with other libraries such as Passport.js, where certain auth strategy middlewares use the `res.redirect` helper internally.

body: @christianalfoni Sorry, left some comments a bit late. I've been working on a demo to showcase Stitches SSR and CRP and have been referring to this. After a while of having some unexpected rendering issues, I decided to clone this and test here as well. At first it worked fine, until I realised this project and mine had different versions of Next.js. This uses Next v9.3.5 and I was using v9.4.4. Changing this to use Next v9.4 surfaces the same issues I'm having, which is: - Make a change - HMR kicks in and applies new styles - Refresh browser twice - Styles are gone ![stitches-next](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/372831/86741462-b0ca3e80-c037-11ea-8ca2-d364a57e0edb.gif) ![CleanShot 2020-07-07 at 09 53 09@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/372831/86741452-adcf4e00-c037-11ea-9a98-49dcd697be28.png) --- Also: it looks like the css vars and being defined twice, had you noticed that too?

body:
> @iamsharzil  Hi there thank you for the PR and sorry for the late review!
> 
> I have never used Magento before and the readme assumes that I have a Magento account (which I don't), can you share a live demo of the example that I can review? 
> 
> If hosting Magento is not free (I did a small research and looks like there aren't good free options) then I would like to review a demo before digging more deep into the example.

@lfades Hi Luis, Can you please tell me how and what would you like to see in the live demo? 
I created this example with the staging environment of my client's account. But if you would want I can share a video explaining the Magento side steps. Please let me know I'm happy to share it with you.
author: iamsharzil

body: @iamsharzil We don't have any other e-commerce examples with the exception of this open PR for a shopify example: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/15137 - It has a demo available (https://nextjs-shopify.vercel.app/) - I would like to see something like that or better. Ideally I would like to see something that would make me want to use Magento, but that starts with a live demo I can review 🙏

body: 🤔  This is causing redirect loops on the `trailing-slashes` integration tests
author: Janpot

body:
We might need to keep this strict. We were making this change to fix a bug in `path-to-regexp`:

**Correct**
```
> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('/ab')
true

> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('/ab/')
false

> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:false}).test('/')
true

> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('')
true
```

**Incorrect**
```
> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('/')
false
```

---

Let's fix the bug in `path-to-regexp` instead?
author: Timer

body: Opened issue here https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/issues/228
author: Timer

body: They confirmed the behavior is intentional in case users are passing non-prefixed paths.
author: Timer

body: Closing this PR since the behavior is currently intentional, we misunderstood how it should work.

body:
@isaachinman Wouldn't using namespaces solve that?

Anyway, here's my use case for context:
1. I didn't want to bundle my translations in the `public/` folder and send the entire translation json files to the client's browser.
2. I didn't want any language specifc routes in my application like `/en` or `/de`.
3. I wanted to use hooks for translations since they're straightforward and don't require me to add any additional components in my code. That's the primary reason I avoided `react-intl`.
4. I had no use for an i18n backend or language detector. Setting the default language in i18n config works fine.

It took me several days to figure out `react-i18next` can even work with `Next.js` without setting up Express or using something like `rosetta` or `redirects()`. This example would've made life much easier if it was present in Next.js repo before I started so I decided to make a minimal example and send a PR.

Please let me know if this adds any caveats that I need to mention in the readme. But for my particular use case, this is the exact example I was looking for. Just straightforward translations with `react-i18next`, nothing else needed.

author: isaachinman

body:
@isaachinman That sounds awesome! I've been waiting for `rewrites()` to be released as stable for some time now so we can use it in production and stop depending on Express to do API routing. ( Related: #14634 )

Regarding `react-i18next`, I believe there should be an example available on how to use it directly. `Next.js` is awesome, but people using it are still React developers and search for "How to do this with React" first before searching "How to do this with Next.js".

This was the case with me. Searched for translations with React, found `react-i18next`, added the code to my `Next.js` project, and after hours realized that their official example doesn't work with `Next.js`. Almost migrated my entire project to Razzle in frustration before realizing there was this workaround.

Regarding `next-i18next`, perhaps the serverless example reference can be added to the `Next.js` or `react-i18next` tutorial or docs so it's easier to stumble into?

body:
@cseas The example you've submitted with this PR is not something which people should take guidance from, in my opinion. It _works_, yes, but there are many antipatterns that will cause serious issues for projects of any reasonable size. As you have found out, it is indeed possible to use `react-i18next` directly with NextJs and make things _work_, but once you look into it any deeper than surface level, you will realise that it's actually a semi-complex problem to solve. That's why `next-i18next` and various other packages exist.

Just one example – in your example app here, an English user would end up downloading all German translations, despite never needing them. In fact, it looks like every user would download every language, and every namespace.
author: isaachinman

body:
@isaachinman Ah, got it. Would that be because of using the `resources` instead of a `Backend` in `i18n` `init()` and just the way `i18n` works? Or is this specific to `Next.js` and using `resources` is fine otherwise?

I didn't really understand what benefits the http backend gives to i18n over just importing the json files. Is there any documentation available that would cover this explanation?
author: cseas

body:
Correct. The docs are on the [repo](https://github.com/i18next/i18next-http-backend).

We need some kind of resource backend to fetch assets per language and per namespace, as needed. In a NextJs context, we may introduce new language or namespace requirements on the client side after a new component mounts, or the route changes. You can see logic to cover the route change case in `next-i18next` [here](https://github.com/isaachinman/next-i18next/blob/master/src/hocs/app-with-translation.tsx#L57), for example.

To summarise my view on i18n in NextJs: unless you are a large org that has the desire and capacity to roll your own solution, you should probably just grab an off-the-shelf solution, as it will save you a lot of time and headache in the long run. I think that promoting these "simple i18n" examples is actually a disservice to new devs, and I have seen this same pattern play out countless times in the past couple years.
author: isaachinman

body: @cseas Okay with closing the PR based on @isaachinman comments? I agree with him and the current state of the example is not ideal. `rewrites` are going to be released in the next stable release as everything for them is ready, including the docs.
author: lfades

body:
@lfades Yeah that sounds alright. I still wish `Next.js` supported other libraries that React projects usually do though. This is just a beginner's perspective but coming from `create-react-app` or a custom `webpack` toolchain, it really feels like a paradigm shift trying to switch to `Next.js` to get server-side rendering. React router doesn't work, react-i18next is discouraged, and idk how many more of these replacements do I have to learn for a switch.

I like the features of Next and wish I could promote it where I work. But the concept of "use only Next libraries for everything" feels too restrictive as a developer. I might give Razzle a try, still exploring options for a new project.

author: ijjk

body:
Been doing a some digging today and the test issue has already occurred [once before](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/12952) it seems, where the result has been that @StarpTech has submitted a [pull request](https://github.com/michael-ciniawsky/postcss-load-plugins/pull/119) to [postcss-load-plugins](https://github.com/michael-ciniawsky/postcss-load-plugins), which now has been two months stale. The proposed changes would hopefully result in code that is easier to follow, but I still think that it would requires some change in [styled-jsx-plugin-postcss](https://github.com/giuseppeg/styled-jsx-plugin-postcss) to get it working all the way through. 

I am still uncertain of why the bug happens in the first place. I tried running the styledstyled-jsx-plugin-postcss through the next babel preset with the different versions of babel and they both came out identical from what I could see.

If anyone has some pointers on where to look next (pun-intended) I'll see if I can find the time :)
author: Bjodol

body:
Hi @Bjodol are you still working on this PR? There are some conflicts but next@canary hasn't updated yet to babel 7.10. You can run the styled-jsx tests locally and see why they broke:

```bash
yarn testonly --testPathPattern=integration/styled-jsx-plugin
```

See [contributing.md](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/contributing.md) for more detailed steps.

body:
@lfades do you mean the posts inside the posts folder, like `blog-starter-mdx/pages/posts/foo-bar.mdx`? I tried this approach (it is actually what I am doing now with my blog) and I didn't like it so far for these reasons:
1. the posts are all inside the `pages/posts` folder, imo it is more organized at the top level like in the `blog-starter` example
2. all the posts have the same layout boilerplate (import and exporting the component), I don't mind it too much but it is still a negative point
3. all pages have the "layout code" inside `pages/`, but the posts are the only exception where the layout has to be outside the pages folder 

The downside of the solution of this PR is the little fact that HMR doesn't work at all, lol

Both solutions are able to use all the advantages of MDX, with exception of imports inside the MDX source that isn't a big deal since you can still inject the custom components like I did with the `Counter` in this example. So both solutions have trade-offs

With all that said, I am happy to change to the pages approach if you think it is better as an example, we can still document the `next-mdx-remote` approach in the README
